what: No documented way to get the CB-allocatable L1 budget from Python. device.l1_size_per_core() does not exist on MeshDevice; GetAllocatorBaseAddress lives at ttnn._ttnn.device (not ttnn.device); ttnn.get_max_worker_l1_unreserved_size() (1531776 B on BH) overstates the real CB region (allocator base 111744 B, bank 1461120 B) by ~70 KB, which overflowed L1 at program build on a sized-to-fit plan
suggest: Document the L1 budget query: ttnn._ttnn.device.GetMemoryView(device, ttnn.BufferType.L1).total_bytes_per_bank clipped by the lowest allocated block address (or GetAllocatorBaseAddress + bank size); warn that get_max_worker_l1_unreserved_size is not the CB budget

what: The mcast host API does not say which NoC a WriterConfigDescriptor / ReaderConfigDescriptor kernel resolves to. Writers resolve to NOC_1 (preferred_noc_for_dram_write), so McastConfig(noc=NOC_0) on a writer kernel trips TT_FATAL noc == cfg_.noc at attach; the design (and CLAUDE.md wording) implied the writer uses NOC_0
suggest: In mcast.hpp/README, state that McastConfig.noc must equal the target kernel NoC: ReaderConfig -> NOC_0, WriterConfig -> NOC_1, or use DataMovementConfigDescriptor with an explicit noc

what: The design specifies input(A, WaitPolicy::PerTile, PopPolicy::PerTile, InputTileMapping::Block) for the streamed normalize operand, which the eltwise chain rejects (is_legal_input_policy_for_mapping: Block needs Upfront/None/Cumulative/PerBlockSize; PerTile streaming needs Scalar)
suggest: Planner prompt or chain.hpp InputTileMapping docs: include a short legal (Wait,Pop)x(Mapping) table so designs only name legal combos
